title: Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation
text_A: The DAR, in coordination with other relevant agencies, shall provide as much as possible, support to all Agrarian Reform Communities (ARCs) to strengthen their climate resilience, including the conduct of climate and disaster risk assessments, provision of capacity-building on value-adding activities and non-farm livelihood options, enhancing access to innovative agricultural insurance coverage such as weather index-based insurance, and enhancing their capacity to adopt climate-resilient technologies. The DAR, in coordination with other relevant agencies, shall also capacitate the ARCs in the use of renewable energy and energy efficiency, ecological solid waste management, and sustainable land use such as organic farming approaches, and the use of rainwater catchments.

title: Competitiveness Enhancement Measures Fund
text_A: In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the amount chargeable against the SAGF reflected in the BESF Table B.15 under the FY 2027 Proposed Expenditures shall be earmarked for competitiveness enhancement measures for agri-fishery industries affected by increased imports, sourced from fifty percent (50%) of the revenues collected from fees, charges, and safeguard duties, constituted into the Competitiveness Enhancement Measures Fund in accordance with Section 34 of R.A. No. 8800: Provided , That such fund shall be utilized for the implementation of agricultural and fisheries programs, projects, and activities that promote competitiveness, such as, but not limited to, the following: (i) development and accreditation of nurseries for plants and stock farms for livestock; (ii) organization of farmers into cooperatives and associations, especially those engaged in coffee farming; (iii) selection and distribution of site- specific planting varieties; (iv) repopulation and enhancement of multiplier farms; (v) establishment of postharvest facilities; and (vi) provision of market access and branding support. Administration of the fund shall be subject to DA-DTI J.M.C. No. 23-01 dated March 22, 2023, and such other guidelines that may be issued for the purpose. title: Quick Response Fund
text_A: The amount of One Billion Pesos (P1,000,000,000) appropriated herein for the Quick Response Fund (QRF) shall serve as a stand-by fund to be used for: (i) provision of various production inputs for crops, livestock, and poultry; (ii) repair of production, post-production facilities, small-scale irrigation systems, equipment, and machinery; (iii) provision of other assistance in the form of cash for culled live animals, and fuel assistance to farmers, subject to guidelines issued by the DA; and (iv) provision of necessary tools and supplies directly used to mitigate the effects of an ongoing disaster, in order that the situation and living conditions of people in communities or areas affected by natural or human-induced calamities, epidemics, crises and catastrophes, which occurred in the last quarter of the immediately preceding year and those occurring during the current year may be normalized as quickly as possible. In no case shall the QRF be used for pre-disaster activities, such as conduct of training, insurance of assets, and public information and education initiatives, or any other purpose not authorized in this provision. Utilization of the QRF shall be subject to DBM-OCD J.C. No. 2025-01 dated April 2, 2025, and such other guidelines as may be issued by the OCD and DBM.

title: Farm-to-Market Road Projects
text_A: The amount of Sixteen Billion Pesos (P16,000,000,000) appropriated herein for Farm-to-Market Road (FMR) projects shall be used for the construction, improvement, rehabilitation, and repair of FMRs in accordance with the National FMR Network Plan (2023-2028). For this purpose, the DA through its Bureau of Agriculture and Fisheries Engineering (BAFE) and Regional Field Units (RFUs) shall undertake the planning and implementation of the program and may enter into a MOA with the DPWH, qualified LGUs or through Public Private Partnerships. The DA shall ensure that: (i) the FMR network plan shall include the scope of work, estimated length in kilometers, and specific location for each of the FMR projects, as well as a list of priority FMR projects, which must lead to arterial or secondary roads and key production areas; (ii) the detailed engineering design and program of works have passed technical review; (iii) prior to the procurement of any FMR project, the approved budget for the contract is subjected to cost validation by the DA-BAFE, taking into account prevailing market prices, standard unit costs, and site-specific conditions; and (iv) the FMRs implemented are properly geo-tagged. The approved FMR network plan shall be regularly updated to prioritize: (i) major rice, corn, high value commercial crops, livestock, and fishery producing provinces; (ii) areas where the majority of small farmers and agrarian reform beneficiaries registered under the RSBSA are located; and (iii) provinces or regions where the absolute number of poor farmers and the incidence of poverty are high as identified in the latest official poverty statistics of the PSA. Upon completion of the construction, improvement, rehabilitation, and repair of FMRs, the DA shall turn over the management and ownership thereof to the LGUs concerned, which shall commit to shoulder the maintenance and repair costs. Implementation of FMR projects shall be subject to DA A.0. No. 4 dated March 6, 2026 and such other guidelines as may be issued by the DA. The DA shall maintain and regularly update a publicly accessible online dashboard on its official website containing information on FMR projects, including but not limited to the project timeline and status of each project, location, list of contracts awarded and corresponding contractors, funding source, amounts obligated and disbursed, and such other relevant details as may be necessary to ensure transparency and accountability. The DA-BAFE shall, within thirty (30) days after the end of each quarter, submit to the House Committee on Appropriations and the Senate Committee on Finance, a report on the status and implementation of FMR projects, including financial and physical accomplishments and issues affecting implementation. The details of the FMR projects, including the coordinates, are provided in Volume I-B of this Act.

text_A: The DA is authorized to deduct engineering and administrative overhead (EAO) expenses not exceeding one percent (1%) of the project funds for small-scale irrigation projects, and other infrastructure projects costing more than One Million Pesos (P1,000,000). title: Basic Education Facilities
text_A:
The amount of Thirty Billion Five Hundred Fifty One Million Sixteen Thousand Pesos (P30,551,016,000) appropriated herein under the Basic Education Facilities shall be used for the construction, replacement, reconstruction, repair, rehabilitation, retrofitting, renovation, restoration, and completion of kindergarten, elementary, and secondary school buildings, including site improvements, categorized under the following components: (a) Low-rise School Buildings; (b) Medium-rise School Buildings; (c) Last Mile School; (d) Gabaldon and other Heritage School Buildings; (e) Technical-Vocational Laboratories; (f) Library and Innovation Hubs; (g) Inclusive Learning Resource Centers; and (h) Alternative Learning System (ALS) - Community Learning Centers. In addition, the DepEd shall ensure that the Gabaldon and Other Heritage School Buildings are fully restored according to the standards set in the IRR of R.A. No. 11194. For this purpose, the DepEd shall coordinate with the National Commission for Culture and the Arts, the National Historical Commission of the Philippines, and the National Museum of the Philippines for a review of the list of Gabaldon school buildings to be conserved and restored. Likewise, the said fund may be used for the following: (i) Conduct and revision of preliminary and detailed engineering activities such as site validation, subsoil exploration, perimeter survey, and geotechnical evaluation; (ii) Construction, replacement, repair, rehabilitation of water systems, handwashing facilities, toilet facilities, and other health and sanitation-related facilities of the
schools and their adaptation for accessibility of persons with disabilities to prevent disease transmission and ensure school sanitation; and (iii) Acquisition of school desks, furniture, and fixtures to ensure that all newly constructed and existing kindergarten, elementary, and secondary school buildings are
provided with the corresponding number of school desks, furniture, and fixtures. In the implementation of this provision, the DepEd may enter into a MOA with other government agencies, such as the DPWH, qualified LGUs, and the AFP Corps of Engineers: Provided, That the implementation by the LGUs shall be subject to the General Provision on the Implementation of Nationally Funded Projects under this Act. The DepEd may likewise enter into a MOA with Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) or Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) for the construction of school buildings or engage a contractor to implement the same but without any profit margin or mark-up on the part of the CSO or NGO, subject to the General Provision on the Fund Transfers to Civil Society Organizations under this Act. For this purpose, the DepEd shall identify the legal, technical and financial requirements to be complied by the CSOs or NGOs. In any case, the CSO or NGO shall remain responsible and accountable to DepEd in the implementation of the project. To ensure timely implementation, DepEd or its authorized partner implementing agencies may conduct early procurement activities, short of award, in accordance with applicable laws, rules, and regulations. Provided, That not more than one percent (1%) of this fund shall be used for engineering and administrative overhead (EAO) expenses which shall be limited to: (i) administrative overhead including the hiring of individuals engaged through job orders or contracts of service or such other engagement of personnel without employer- employee relationship; (ii) pre-construction activities after detailed engineering or pre-repair/rehabilitation activities such as conduct of necessary structural test to determine the condition of the structure and the appropriate repair/rehabilitation needs; (iii) project management including the conduct of regular monitoring to ensure quality and timely completion of the projects; (iv) testing and quality control; (v) acquisition, rehabilitation, and repair of related equipment and parts; and (vi) contingencies in relation to pre-construction/repair/rehabilitation activities. The EAO expenses shall be treated or booked-up as capitalized expenditures and form part of the project cost.

title: Creation of Teaching Positions, Recruitment, and Appointment of Teachers
text_A:

Organization, Staffing and Compensation Action (NOSCA); (c) Selection of teachers based on the Comparative Assessment Results - Registry of Qualified Applicants and their subsequent appointment upon issuance of the
NOSCA with priority given to those previously created but remained unfilled; and (d) Assignment of teachers by schools division which shall be identified as their station. Teachers may be transferred within their station to address the imbalances
resulting from excess or shortage of teachers by reason of increase or decrease in enrollment. title: Government Assistance and Subsidies
text_A: The amount of Thirty Eight Billion One Hundred Twenty Two Million Four Hundred Ninety Four Thousand Pesos (P38,122,494,000) appropriated herein for Government Assistance and Subsidies (GAS) shall be allocated for the implementation of Educational Service Contracting (ESC) Program, Senior High School (SHS) Voucher Program, and Joint Delivery Voucher Program (JDVP). The implementation of the ESC and SHS Voucher Programs, as well as other programs of GAS, including the conduct of research towards the attainment of the objectives of government assistance to private education, shall be subject to the issuance of policies and guidelines by DepEd. The JDVP shall be managed by the DepEd while the ESC and SHS Voucher Programs, as well as other programs of GAS, shall be managed jointly by DepEd and the Private Education Assistance Committee (PEAC). Implementation of the above-mentioned programs with government agencies and other institutions such as TESDA may also be allowed. The DepEd shall also ensure that assistance and voucher amounts be regularly reviewed and updated by the State Assistance Council (SAC). The DepEd shall convene the SAC and shall develop guidelines to regularly update government assistance and voucher amounts that will sufficiently support the transfer of public school students to private schools. The DepEd shall ensure that a list of the schools and institutions participating in ESC and SHS Voucher Programs, and JDVP, respectively, is posted on the DepEd website. For programs managed jointly with PEAC, the respective lists shall also be posted on the PEAC website. The DepEd shall continue to implement the GAS Programs for beneficiaries - learners, teachers, and schools - in the BARMM. The implementation of this Program, including the monitoring of payment to BARMM schools, shall be subject to the guidelines to be issued by DepEd.
text_B: The amount of Forty Billion Fifty Four Million Seven Hundred Nineteen Thousand Pesos (P40,054,719,000) appropriated herein for Government Assistance and Subsidies (GAS) shall be allocated for the implementation of Educational Service Contracting (ESC) Program, Senior High School (SHS) Voucher Program, and Joint Delivery Voucher Program (JDVP) and other related government assistance programs such as the GAS-TUKLAS and the Kindergarten to Grade 6 Subsidy (K to 6 Subsidy), subject to existing budgeting, accounting, and auditing rules, and regulations. The implementation of the ESC and SHS Voucher Programs, as well as other programs of GAS, including the conduct of research towards the attainment of the objectives of government assistance to private education, shall be subject to the issuance of policies and guidelines by DepEd. The JDVP and GAS-TUKLAS shall be managed by the DepEd while the ESC, SHS Voucher Program, and the K to 6 Subsidy Program may be implemented by DepEd jointly with qualified government entities or private entities: Provided, That where no such entity is available or engaged, DepEd may partner with the Private Education Assistance Committee (PEAC) for such purpose. The engagement of private entities shall be subject to applicable procurement laws and regulations and the audit jurisdiction of the Commission on Audit. The DepEd shall regularly review and update the assistance and voucher amounts, taking into consideration prevailing costs of basic education, fiscal capacity, and other relevant factors, to ensure adequate support for eligible learners enrolled in participating private basic education institutions. Qualified beneficiaries shall be allowed to select their preferred school from a registry of participating private basic education institutions, subject to eligibility, accessibility, and other requirements. The DepEd shall ensure that a list of the schools and institutions participating in ESC, SHS Voucher Program, JDVP, and K to 6 Subsidy Program is posted on the DepEd website. For programs managed jointly with PEAC, the respective lists shall also be posted on the PEAC website. The DepEd shall continue to implement the GAS Programs for beneficiaries - learners, teachers, and schools - in the BARMM.

title: School-Based Feeding Program (SBFP)
text_A: The amount appropriated herein shall be used to provide nutritious food to all incoming kindergarten, and wasted, severely wasted, and stunted, and severely stunted grades one to six learners as determined by the DepEd in its reports, pupils-at-risk of dropping out, indigenous people learners, and those coming from indigent families. dept_printed: DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENT AND NATURAL RESOURCES
title: Adaptation of Nature-Based Solution
text_A: The DENR shall ensure that nature-based solutions form an essential component of national environmental policy and flood mitigation strategy. All programs, projects, and activities related to watershed management, river and wetland rehabilitation, coastal protection, reforestation, land restoration, and climate adaptation shall incorporate nature-based approaches, whenever technically feasible and ecologically appropriate. The DENR shall prioritize interventions such as native-species reforestation, assisted natural regeneration, bamboo and vetiver stabilization, contour farming, and the establishment of catchment ponds to restore degraded uplands and strengthen watershed functions. The DENR shall likewise protect forests from illegal logging, mining, encroachment, and land conversion, and rehabilitate rivers, riparian buffers, wetlands, and floodplains to allow natural water retention and reduce downstream flooding. In urban areas, the DENR shall support the use of green and sponge-city infrastructure, including permeable pavements, bioswales, rain gardens, rainwater harvesting systems, retention parks, and green roofs, alongside the strict enforcement of solid waste laws to prevent waterway obstruction and restore natural drainage systems. For coastal zones, the DENR shall prioritize the restoration and protection of mangroves, beach forests, dunes, and seagrass beds as natural defenses against storm surge, coastal erosion, and saline intrusion. All planning and implementation shall be aligned with an integrated flood management and river basin framework and guided by updated multi-hazard maps to ensure that interventions are science-based, risk-informed, and climate-aligned. The DENR shall submit to Congress, within the first quarter of the ensuing year, an annual report detailing the integration of nature-based solutions into its key programs, including accomplishments, challenges, and recommendations for further policy and institutional strengthening.

dept_printed: DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENT AND NATURAL RESOURCES
title: Implementation of Early Warning Systems for Water Infrastructure
text_A: The DENR, in coordination with the Climate Change Commission (CCC), Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH), Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG), and Department of Science and Technology (DOST), shall implement early warning systems and forecasting tools to anticipate potential challenges related to water shortages, contamination, and infrastructure damage caused by climate change-related disasters.
text_B: The DENR, in coordination with the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH), Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG), and Department of Science and Technology (DOST), and other concerned implementing agencies, shall strengthen the implementation of early warning systems and forecasting tools to anticipate potential risks related to water shortages, droughts, flooding, contamination, and extreme rainfall arising from climate and disaster-related hazards. Such systems shall, where applicable, utilize available climate projections, hydrological, watershed, geohazard, and multi-hazard risk information and shall support preparedness, anticipatory action, climate-resilient water resource management, and infrastructure planning. Relevant information generated from early warning and forecasting systems shall, where appropriate, be integrated into CCIMS and made available to concerned national government agencies and LGUs to support risk-informed planning, programming, and decision-making.

dept_printed: DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENT AND NATURAL RESOURCES
title: Identification, Assessment, and Monitoring of Vulnerable Habitats
text_A: The DENR, in coordination with the CCC, shall conduct regular identification, assessment, and monitoring of vulnerable habitats and ecosystems to ensure timely protection against degradation resulting from both natural and anthropogenic activities. Further, the DENR shall implement rehabilitation measures for critical habitats and ecosystems and enhance ecosystem service outputs in response to climate hazards. The DENR shall closely coordinate with the Department of Economy, Planning, and Development (DEPDev) in ensuring convergence with the implementation of R.A. No. 11995 or the Philippine Ecosystem and Natural Capital Accounting System (PENCAS) Act.
text_B: The DENR shall conduct regular identification, assessment, and monitoring of vulnerable habitats and ecosystems to ensure timely protection against degradation resulting from both natural and anthropogenic activities and climate- and disaster- related hazards. The DENR shall implement appropriate protection, rehabilitation, restoration, and nature-based measures for critical habitats and ecosystems to maintain and enhance ecosystem services and resilience. The DENR shall closely coordinate with the Department of Economy, Planning, and Development (DEPDev) to ensure convergence with R.A. No. 11995 or the Philippine Ecosystem and Natural Capital Accounting System (PENCAS) Act, particularly in the use of ecosystem and natural capital information for climate-resilient planning, recovery, and investment decision-making.

dept_printed: DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENT AND NATURAL RESOURCES
title: Unified River Basin and Flood Management Database
text_A: The DENR, in coordination with the DPWH, shall jointly develop and maintain a unified river basin and flood management database to support integrated and science-based planning for watershed rehabilitation. Such coordination shall ensure that flood control projects complement environmental protection and climate resilience goals.
text_B: The DENR, in coordination with DPWH, shall jointly develop, maintain, and enhance a unified river basin and flood management database to support integrated, science-based, and climate- and disaster-risk-informed planning for watershed rehabilitation, river basin management, flood risk reduction, and climate-resilient development. Such coordination shall ensure that flood control and other water-related infrastructure interventions complement watershed protection and rehabilitation, ecosystem integrity, nature-based solutions, disaster risk reduction, and climate resilience objectives.

title: Fees and Other Receipts of the Securities and Exchange Commission
text_A: The amount collected by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) from fees, fines, and other charges pursuant to R.A. No. 11232 and its rules and regulations, shall be deposited and maintained in a separate account to be used for its modernization and to augment its operational expenses such as, but not limited to, Capital Outlays, increase in compensation and benefits comparable with prevailing rates in the private sector, reasonable employee allowance, employee health care service and other insurance, employee career advancement and professionalization, legal assistance, seminars and other professional fees in accordance with Section 175 of the said law. In addition, the SEC is authorized to retain and utilize the amount of One Hundred Million Pesos (P100,000,000) from its income from the registration of securities and other collection pursuant to R.A. No. 8799. The use of income shall be in accordance with DBM-SEC J.C. No. 1 dated September 8, 2020, and such other guidelines issued thereon. Disbursements or expenditures by the SEC in violation of the above requirements shall be void and shall subject the erring officials and employees to disciplinary actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5, and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, s. 1987, and to appropriate civil and criminal actions under existing laws. The SEC shall prepare and submit to the DBM not later than November 15 of the preceding year, the annual operating budget for the current fiscal year covering its retained income and the corresponding expenditures. Likewise, it shall submit to the DBM not later than March 1 of the current year its audited financial statements for the immediately preceding year.

title: Tax Refund
text_A:
The amount of Twenty Billion Fifty Eight Million Nine Hundred Fifty Thousand Pesos (P20,058,950,000) shall be used for the following: (a) Refund of excess or erroneous collection of value-added tax (VAT) and other internal revenue taxes in accordance with Section 229 of R.A. No. 8424, as amended,
including legal interest thereon treated as related expense; (b) Refund of excess collections of duties pursuant to Title IX of R.A. No. 10863; (c) Cash conversion of valid and unexpired Tax Credit Certificates (TCCs) in accordance with Section 204 of R.A. No. 8424, as amended; and (d) Refund of input taxes attributable to zero-rated or effectively zero-rated transactions under Section 112 of R.A. No. 8424, as amended. The amount intended for the payment of VAT refunds shall be limited to five percent (5%) of the total VAT collections of the BOC from the immediately preceding year, while those for payment of the other tax refunds shall be sourced from the current year's tax revenue collections of the BOC. All tax refund payments shall be subject to the following: (i) adjustment of the report on BOC's tax revenue collections equivalent to the tax refunds for current and prior years; and (ii) COA audit. The amount herein shall be treated as trust receipts, subject to reversion of any unutilized amount at the end of the year to the unappropriated surplus of the General Fund in accordance with Section 31 of R.A. No. 10963 and Section 45, Chapter 5, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, s. 1987. Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements in accordance with applicable laws, rules, and regulations.

title: Disposition of Forfeited Motor Transport Equipment and Other Articles
text_A: Motor transport equipment and other articles forfeited or abandoned in favor of the government shall be sold at public auction by the BOC upon approval by the DOF. The proceeds of the sale shall be deposited with the National Treasury as income of the General Fund in accordance with Section 44, Chapter 5, Book VI of E.O. No. 292. Any government agency participating in the said auction shall pay out of its programmed budget for the purpose, subject to the rules and regulations on the acquisition and use of government motor vehicles. The Commissioner of Customs and the Bureau's web administrator or his/her equivalent shall be responsible for ensuring that the list of forfeited or abandoned motor equipment and other articles that have been sold in auction are posted on the BOC's website.

title: Building Fund
text_A:
The amount of One Billion Four Hundred Million Pesos (P1,400,000,000) appropriated herein for the Building Fund shall be used for the following: (a) acquisition or construction of new properties abroad and in the Philippines for chanceries and residences, as well as office space for consular offices through
direct purchase or lease-purchase agreements; (b) renovation of deteriorating government-owned consular offices, chanceries, and residences of the Philippine Foreign Service, as well as properties under leasehold
agreement for at least twenty (20) years; (c) purchase of furniture, fixtures, and equipment for chanceries, residences, and consular offices; (d) long-term lease of chanceries, residences, and consular offices when the terms and conditions are favorable and advantageous to the government; (e) payment of the services of a highly technical consultant relative to the renovation, redevelopment, and construction of chanceries, residences, and consular

consular offices. The DFA shall consider all previously committed undertakings and the available balance of the Building Fund in the programming for the current year and give preference to the acquisition or construction of properties abroad and renovation of government-owned properties.

title: Health Facilities Enhancement Program
text_A: The amount appropriated herein for the implementation of the Health Facilities Enhancement Program (HFEP) shall be used for the construction, upgrading, or expansion of government health care facilities, and purchase of medical equipment, including equipment for medical ancillary services, and medical transport vehicles for such facilities, with priorities in the construction/completion of ongoing infrastructure projects, the establishment of specialty centers in DOH hospitals, and the construction of Primary Care Facilities (PCFs) in the UHC Integration Sites and GIDAs, the upgrading of other DOH-managed facilities, and the establishment of warehouses and other support infrastructure based on utmost necessity and consistent with R.A. No. 11223. In the implementation of the infrastructure projects and procurement of equipment used for medical purposes and/or required for the delivery of medical ancillary and support services under the HFEP, the DOH may enter into a MOA with the DPWH, other appropriate government agencies, or qualified LGUs in accordance with the General Provision on the Implementation of Nationally Funded Projects under this Act. The DOH may likewise undertake implementation through appropriate Public-Private Partnership (PPP) arrangements. The implementation of the project by the implementing agencies, LGUs, or through PPP must comply with the original project scope, cost, and approved timeline of construction except in cases of unforeseen or fortuitous events, subject to the guidelines to be issued by the DOH specifically for this purpose. The DOH shall promptly transfer or release the funds necessary for the implementation of the projects, subject to the provisions of the MOA and to applicable budgeting, accounting, and auditing laws, rules, and regulations. The transfer of funds for HFEP projects under MOA with Corporate Hospitals and Ministry of Health-BARMM shall be subject to the necessary guidelines to implement this provision, the MOA on the transfer of funds, and the existing budgeting, accounting, and auditing rules and regulations. title: Medical Assistance to Indigent and Financially-Incapacitated Patients
text_A: The amount appropriated herein under Medical Assistance to Indigent and Financially-Incapacitated Patients (MAIFIP) shall be used for hospitalization and medical assistance to indigent or financially incapacitated patients, including but not limited to, inpatient services, outpatient services, comprehensive checkups, emergency services, dental services, drugs and medicines as approved by the FDA, and 100% professional fees, subject to the guidelines issued by the DOH. In no case shall more than one percent (1%) of said amount be used for administrative expenses. The CHDs, through their respective CHD Directors, may enter into a MOA with health facilities such as, but not limited to, DOH hospitals including the four (4) specialty hospitals, SUC hospitals, LGU hospitals, and other medical service providers, including clinical laboratories, primary health care facilities, DOH-accredited dental clinics, and Free-Standing Dialysis Clinics, both private and public. This shall be intended for indigent and financially incapacitated patients to ensure a comprehensive continuum of care, subject to the guidelines issued by the DOH. Likewise, the CHDs may also enter into a MOA with private hospitals and clinical laboratories for health and medical services intended for indigent or financially incapacitated patients, which government hospitals are unable to provide, provided that such services are billed at standard or regulated rates, subject to the guidelines issued by the DOH. The MAIFIP shall also apply to emergency cases handled by private health facilities: Provided, That the private health facility where the patient is brought is the closest in distance and is equipped to provide the life-saving services needed by the patient at the time of emergency, in accordance with the provisions of R.A. No. 8344. Release of subsequent funds for the medical assistance by DOH to specialty, SUC, and LGU hospitals shall be through the CHDs and made only when at least fifty percent (50%) of the amount previously transferred has been liquidated in accordance with accounting and auditing rules and regulations. The DOH, in strict compliance with R.A. No. 10173, shall post on its website the names of recipient hospitals, alongside the aggregated and anonymized data pertaining to the age, gender, city/municipality, and disease profile of recipient indigent and financially incapacitated patients. This shall be utilized for purposes of public accountability, policy formulation, and research, subject to the guidelines to be issued by the DOH.
text_B: The amount appropriated herein under Medical Assistance to Indigent and Financially-Incapacitated Patients (MAIFIP) shall be used for hospitalization and medical assistance to indigent or financially-incapacitated patients, including, but not limited to, in-patient services, outpatient services, comprehensive checkups, emergency services, dental services, ambulatory care services, ophthalmology services, drugs, and medicines as approved by the FDA, and one hundred percent (100%) professional fees, subject to the guidelines issued by the DOH: Provided, That the DOH, in consultation with established medical societies, shall formulate and issue the necessary guidelines to govern the coverage of professional fees under the MAIFIP program. In no case shall more than one percent (1%) of said amount be used for administrative expenses. The Centers for Health Development (CHDs), through their respective CHD Directors, may enter into a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) with health facilities such as, but not limited to, DOH hospitals including the four (4) specialty hospitals, State Universities and Colleges (SUC) hospitals, and Local Government Unit (LGU) hospitals and medical services, including clinical laboratories, primary health care facilities, DOH-accredited dental clinics, Free Standing Dialysis Clinics, ambulatory surgical clinics, and eye centers, both private and public, intended for the indigent and financially-incapacitated patients, subject to the guidelines issued by the DOH. Likewise, the CHDs may also enter into a MOA with private hospitals and clinical laboratories for health and medical services intended for the indigent or financially- incapacitated patients, which the government hospitals are unable to provide, or when government facility capacity is fully exhausted subject to the guidelines issued by the DOH. The medical assistance to indigent or financially-incapacitated patients shall also apply to emergency cases handled by private health facilities: Provided, That the private health facility where the patient is brought is the closest in distance and is able to provide the services needed by the patient at the time of emergency. Release of subsequent funds for the medical assistance by the DOH to specialty, SUC, and LGU hospitals shall be through the DOH Central Office or CHDs and made only when at least twenty five percent (25%) of the amount previously transferred has been liquidated in accordance with accounting and auditing rules and regulations. In the case of unavailability of drugs and medicines, DOH-central office and/or health facilities may enter into a MOA with pharmacies to ensure continued access to drugs and medicines registered with the FDA, including those not listed in the Philippine National Drug Formulary (PNDF) intended for the beneficiaries of the MAIFIP program, subject to relevant laws, rules, and regulations. Unless there is a valid ground for refusal, it shall be unlawful for a health facility, whether public, or private, that has entered into a MOA with the CHD under this special provision, to refuse to accept the referral letter, coupon, check, or voucher issued by the DOH as full or partial payment of the obligation of the qualified beneficiary under the MAIFIP program. The DOH, in strict compliance with R.A. No. 10173 (Data Privacy Act of 2012), shall post on its website the names of recipient hospitals, alongside the aggregated and anonymized data pertaining to the age, gender, city/municipality, and disease profile of recipient indigent and financially incapacitated patients. This shall be utilized for purposes of public accountability, policy formulation, and research, subject to the guidelines to be issued by the DOH.

title: Training for Work Scholarship Program
text_A: The amount of Four Billion Three Hundred Forty Three Milllion One Hundred Forty Seven Thousand Pesos (P4,343,147,000) appropriated herein for the Training for Work Scholarship Program under the Promotion, Development, Implementation, Monitoring, and Evaluation of Technical Education and Skills Development Scholarship and Student Assistance Programs shall be used to support rapid, inclusive, and sustained economic growth through the course offerings to key employment generators in the areas of agri-fishery, agri-business, agro-industrial, tourism, information technology-business process management, semiconductor and electronics, automotives, other priority manufacturing industries, logistics, general infrastructure, and new and emerging sectors and in-demand jobs based on the Latest Market Information Report of the DOLE: Provided , That priority shall be for the training, upskilling, and reskilling of Filipino learners, workers and professionals in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and related technologies, creative industries, semiconductors and electronics manufacturing industry, and healthcare-related programs, including but not limited to pharmacy assistants, dental technologists, medical technologists, radiologic technologists, caregivers, and nurses: Provided , further , That TESDA shall strengthen partnerships with industry, academe, and other government agencies to align the skills development with labor market needs and national priorities, consistent with the current and ongoing strategies. text_A: The amount of One Billion Pesos (P1,000,000,000) appropriated herein for the Quick Response Fund (QRF) shall serve as a stand-by fund to be used for the rehabilitation and relief programs and projects in order that the situation and living conditions of people in communities or areas affected by natural or human-induced calamities, epidemics, crises, and catastrophes, which occurred in the last quarter of the immediately preceding year and those occurring during the current year may be normalized as quickly as possible. dept_printed: DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS
title: Integrated, Environmentally-validated, and Nature-based Flood and Water Resources Management Planning
text_A: The DPWH, in coordination with the DENR, the DEPDev, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council, and other concerned agencies, shall formulate and adopt an Integrated Water Resources and Flood Management Masterplan (IWRFMP) consistent with the principles of Integrated Water Resources Management and ridge-to-reef planning. The IWRFMP shall: (a) integrate all flood-control, drainage, bridge, and road projects into a programmatic, basin-wide, and network-based framework that crosses political and administrative boundaries, ensuring that flood-control infrastructure is planned and implemented as part of an interconnected system rather than as isolated or piecemeal projects; (b) incorporate nature-based and ecosystem-based solutions, such as mangrove reforestation, wetland and river restoration, watershed rehabilitation, and sediment management, as core components of flood mitigation; (c) ensure that all DPWH flood-control and water-related infrastructure projects are supported by scientific hydrologic and geospatial studies, vulnerability assessments, and environmental impact analyses; (d) consult and collaborate with stakeholders and independent experts such as Project Noah and the University of the Philippines Institute of Civil Engineering that can provide scientific and data-driven insights on hydrology, climate modelling, and risk assessments to ensure that flood control plans are technically sound, sustainable, and responsive to community needs; and (e) establish mechanisms for data-sharing, validation, and technical cooperation with development partners such as the Asian Development Bank, Japan International Cooperation Agency, World Bank, and Academnic Institututions to formulate and implement a comprehensive, science-based national flood management strategy.

title: Integration of Active Transportation and Road Transformation in Infrastructure Projects
text_A: Pursuant to E.O. No. 774, s. 2008, NEDA Board Resolution No. 5, s. 2017, the DOH active transport playbook, and all other applicable laws, rules, and regulations, and executive issuances, the DPWH, in coordination with the DOTr and cities where public transport supply is severely insufficient, shall aim to establish proper public transport stops for the benefit of commuters, and ensure that all projects and activities pertaining to the construction, preventive maintenance, rehabilitation, reconstruction, upgrading, off-carriageway improvement, widening, or paving of primary, secondary, tertiary, bypass, and diversion roads, and the construction, widening or replacement of bridges, shall be so designed and implemented as to allocate, insofar as practicable, at least fifty percent (50%) of the road space for public transport, pedestrians, and bicycles/light mobility devices rather than the throughput of private vehicles. All pedestrian crossings and/or footpaths and sidewalks to be constructed in accordance with this provision shall, by default, be at grade for the inclusion of persons with disabilities, senior citizens, pregnant women, children with strollers, tourists with luggage, and parents with children, consistent with public health and safety regulations. For commuter safety and comfort, wherever feasible, all pedestrian and cycling infrastructure to be constructed in accordance with this provision shall be protected or grade-separated and include shaded walkways including urban shade trees, consistent with environmental laws and public health and safety regulations. The DPWH shall, in coordination with DOTr, issue or update policies on road use classification, road space allocation, and road design, in accordance with the National Transport Policy or NEDA Board Resolution No. 5. For infrastructure projects costing more than One Million Pesos (P1,000,000), the DPWH is authorized to deduct, but not to exceed the following percentages of the project cost, to be used for: (i) EAO expenses and (ii) MOOE: (a) three and one half percent (3.5%) for releases to the Central Office; (b) two and one half percent (2.5%) for releases to the Regional Offices (ROs); (c) two percent (2%) for releases to the District Engineering Offices (DEOs); (d) one percent (1%) for infrastructure projects under the Basic Infrastructure Program undertaken by the Central Office, ROs, and DEOs: Provided , That the one
percent (1%) EAO shall be given only to the implementing unit, regardless where the fund was released; or (e) one half percent (0.5%) for infrastructure projects of other agencies undertaken by the Central Office, ROs, or DEOs, unless otherwise provided in the special
provision of the agency concerned. For EAO expenses, the same shall be limited to: (i) administrative overhead including the hiring of individuals engaged through job orders or contracts of service or such other engagement of personnel without any employer-employee relationship; (ii) pre-construction activities after detailed engineering; (iii) construction project management; (iv) testing and quality control; (v) acquisition, rehabilitation, and repair of related equipment and parts; and (vi) contingencies in relation to pre-construction activities. The EAO expenses shall be treated or booked-up as capitalized expenditures and form part of the project cost. Disbursements or expenditures by DPWH in violation of the above requirements shall be void and shall subject the erring officials and employees to disciplinary actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5, and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, and to appropriate civil and criminal action under existing laws.

title: Quick Response Fund
text_A: The amount of One Billion Pesos (P1,000,000,000) appropriated herein for the Quick Response Fund (QRF) shall serve as a stand-by fund to be used for reconstruction and rehabilitation programs, activities, or projects, including pre-positioning of goods and equipment in order that the situation and living conditions of people living in communities or areas stricken by natural or human-induced calamities, epidemics, crises, and catastrophes, which occurred in the last quarter of the immediately preceding year and those occurring during the current year may be normalized as quickly as possible. title: Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program
text_A:
The amount of Ninety Nine Billion Seventy Five Million Four Hundred Ninety Eight Thousand Pesos (P99,075,498,000) appropriated herein for the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps) shall be used to support the poverty reduction and social development strategy of the National Government: Provided , That the 4Ps shall cover the eligible beneficiaries under Section 6 of R.A. No. 11310. The said amount shall cover cash grants, rice subsidy, Enhanced Support Services Intervention (ESSI) grants, and cash grants for the first 1,000-day health monitoring during pregnancy until the child has turned two (2) years old. title: Quick Response Fund
text_A: The amount of One Billion Two Hundred Fifty Million Pesos (P1,250,000,000) appropriated herein for the Quick Response Fund (QRF) shall serve as a stand-by fund to be used for rehabilitation and relief programs, including the pre-positioning of goods and equipment, in order that the situations and living conditions of people in communities or areas affected by natural or human-induced calamities, epidemics, crises, and catastrophes which occurred in the last quarter of the immediately preceding year and those occurring during the current year may be normalized as quickly as possible. In no case shall the QRF be used for pre- disaster activities, such as conduct of training, insurance of assets, and public information and education initiatives, or any other purpose not authorized in this provision. title: Implementation of Shared Service Facilities
text_A: The amount of Four Hundred Sixty Four Million Nine Hundred Twenty Nine Thousand Pesos (P464,929,000) appropriated herein for the implementation of the Shared Service Facilities (SSF) shall be used for projects that aim to improve the quality and productivity of MSMEs. Its implementation shall be primarily based on priority industry clusters identified by the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) in consultation with key stakeholders. Upon the procurement of the machinery and equipment for the SSF, the DTI shall turn over the management thereof to the Cooperators, which shall commit to shoulder maintenance and repair costs upon acceptance thereof. After the period of two (2) years, the DTI may either: (i) transfer ownership of the SSF to the Cooperators that demonstrated successful management of the facilities; (ii) extend the usufruct period for another two (2) years if the Cooperator needs additional period to establish the successful operation of the SSF; or (iii) transfer the management of the SSF equipment to another Cooperator for failure to secure, operate, properly maintain, or repair the SSF equipment upon acceptance.

title: Engineering and Administrative Overhead Expenses
text_A:
The Department of Transportation (DOTr) is authorized to deduct engineering and administrative overhead (EAO) expenses for infrastructure projects costing more than Five Million Pesos (P5,000,000) but not to exceed three percent (3%) of the project cost.
261 The authorized EAO expenses shall be limited to: (i) administrative overhead including the hiring of individuals engaged through job orders or contracts of service or such other engagement of personnel without any employer-employee relationship; (ii) pre-construction activities after detailed engineering; (iii) construction project management; (iv) testing and quality control; (v) acquisition, rehabilitation, and repair of related equipment and parts; and (vi) contingencies in relation to pre-construction activities. The EAO expenses shall be treated or booked-up as capitalized expenditures and form part of the project cost. Disbursements or expenditures by the DOTr in violation of the above requirements shall be void and shall subject the erring officials and employees to disciplinary actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5, and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. title: Active Transport Bike Share System and Safe Pathways Program
text_A: The amount of Thirty Three Million Eight Hundred Fifty Six Thousand Pesos (P33,856,000) appropriated herein for the active transport program shall be used to construct, maintain, and improve protected bike lanes and pedestrian walkways, procure bike racks, construct and improve end-of-trip cycling and other support facilities, and upgrade existing pop-up bike lanes to permanent bike lanes in accordance with DOTr Department Order (D.0.) No. 2020-014, DPWH D.0. No. 263, s. 2022, and other applicable guidelines promoting and prioritizing active transportation. This shall include the planting of urban shade trees consistent with environmental laws. The DOTr, in coordination with the DPWH, shall also establish proper public transport stops for the benefit of commuters, and ensure that all projects pertaining to the construction, preventive maintenance, rehabilitation, reconstruction, upgrading, off-carriageway improvement, widening and/or paving of primary, secondary, tertiary, bypass and diversion roads, and the construction, widening, or replacement of bridges, shall be so designed and implemented so as to allocate, insofar as practicable, at least fifty percent (50%) of the road space for public transport, pedestrians, and bicycles/light mobility devices. Bike lanes should have smooth pavement, be free of hazards, and with durable physical separation from mixed traffic lanes. Pedestrian walkways and pedestrian crossings shall, by default, be at-grade for the inclusion of persons with disability (PWD), senior citizens, pregnant women, children with strollers, tourists with luggage, and parents with children. For commuter safety and comfort, pedestrian and cycling infrastructure shall be protected or grade-separated and include shaded walkways and urban shade trees wherever feasible.

title: Public Transport Modernization Program
text_A:

technologies, including battery electric vehicles (BEVs), and units designed or retrofitted to be accessible to PWD as well as the development or support of
associated depot-based or terminal-based charging facilities necessary for the operation of such electric fleets; (f) Financing; (g) Stakeholder support mechanism; (h) Communications; and (i) Monitoring and evaluation. title: Rationalization of State Universities and Colleges and Local Universities and Colleges Programs and Course Offerings
text_A: The CHED shall evaluate and rationalize all existing programs and course offerings of the SUCs and local universities and colleges (LUCs), particularly LUCs-beneficiaries of R.A. No. 10931, prioritizing programs which are oversubscribed or programs identified by the National Government to be priority programs, to ensure that they are directly aligned with the SUCs'/LUCs' core mandate, consistent with its supervisory and regulatory functions. The CHED shall also ensure that the number of students admitted by the SUCs and LUCs does not exceed the optimal number of students that can be enrolled in each program offered and the number of students that the existing resources and capacity of the SUCs and LUCs can carry, based on predetermined parameters to be determined by the CHED. The CHED shall likewise evaluate applications for the opening of new programs and course offerings if they are within the core mandate of the SUCs/LUCs or fall under the fields of the priority programs.

title: Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education
text_A: The amount appropriated for Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education (UAQTE) shall be used to cover the cost of tertiary education for all Filipino students enrolled in SUCs, LUCs, and private higher education institutions (HEIs), subject to prioritization and availability of funds, pursuant to R.A. No. 10931 and its IRR: (a) For the Implementation of the TES which shall likewise cover the existing grantee under the Tulong Dunong Program. A list of participating HEIs in the TES shall be posted in the Unified Student Financial Assistance System for Tertiary Education (UniFast) website: Provided, That the implementation thereof shall be subject to the guidelines issued by the UniFast Board. The UniFast Board shall administer the amount appropriate herein: Provided, That the same shall be used to cover tuition and other school fees based on 2024 rates: Provided, further, That in no case shall more than one and a half percent (1.5%) of the amount for TES and student loan program be used for administrative cost. (b) For the implementation of the Free Higher Education (FHE), as determined by the respectivegovernng boards of LUCs based on the actual number of enrollees for each academic year, shall be immediately released to such LUCs: Provided, That such determination of the actiual number of enrollees and the amount to be reimbursed shall be subject to the validation of CHED. The CHED shall ensure that the enrollment capacity is strictly observed by the LUCs in the implementation of this Program. In the case of SUCs, the FHE Program of the UAQTE shall be lodged in their respective budgets.

title: Bagong Pilipinas Merit Scholarship Program
text_A: The amount of One Billion Five Hundred Eighty Nine Million Seven Hundred Thirty Seven Thousand Pesos (P1,589,737,000) appropriated herein under the Provision of Assistance and Incentives, Scholarships and Grants through Student Financial Assistance Programs shall be used for the implementation of the Bagong Pilipinas Merit Scholarship Program as educational support for ongoing and incoming college students. title: Implementation of the PAMANA Program
text_A:
The amount of Six Billion Ninety Million Two Hundred Ninety Thousand Pesos (P6,090,290,000) appropriated herein for the PAMANA Program shall be used exclusively by OPAPRU to implement the following projects in conflict-affected and conflict-vulnerable areas:
Project/Expenditure Amount
Agricultural Productivity Support P 77,900,000
Bridge 375,500,000
Community Infrastructure 377,000,000
Electrification 110,250,000
Housing 40,000,000
Road 3,762,750,000
Water Supply System 181,600,000
Social Protection 258,565,000
Implementation Support 75,000,000
Educational Assistance 807,500,000
Educational Assistance Administrative Support 24,225,000
Total P 6,090,290,000 In no case shall these amounts be used for any purpose other than those specifically identified herein. Of the Five Billion Pesos (P5,000,000,000) allotted above for infrastructure projects, the OPAPRU shall be allowed to utilize not more than one and one half percent (1.5%) for coordination, monitoring, and evaluation activities. Of the amounts appropriated herein, Eight Hundred Seven Million Five Hundred Thousand Pesos (P807,500,000) shall be used for the implementation of the Educational Assistance Program (EAP) by SUCs and/or Local Universities and Colleges (LUCs), as endorsed by the OPAPRU through a MOA and Twenty Four Million Two Hundred Twenty Five Thousand Pesos (P24,225,000) shall be used exclusively as administrative cost for monitoring and evaluation. In the implementation of the projects, the OPAPRU may enter into a MOA with the DPWH, SUCs, or other appropriate government agency, or LGU with capability to implement the project, subject to the General Provision on the Implementation of Nationally Funded Projects under this Act.

title: Basic and Meal Allowances of Athletes
text_A:
The PSC shall ensure that all qualified national athletes are uniformly granted basic and meal allowances which should be charged against the NSDF. For this purpose, regular national athletes shall receive the monthly meal allowance of Five Thousand Pesos (P5,000), in addition to the basic training allowance which shall be based on their classification, as follows: (a) Class A - Thirty Thousand Pesos (P30,000); (b) Class B - Twenty Seven Thousand Pesos (P27,000); (c) Class C - (i) Silver Medalist - Twenty Four Thousand Pesos (P24,000); and (ii) Bronze Medalist - Twenty One Thousand Pesos (P21,000); (d) Class C (Team Sports) - Medalist - Seventeen Thousand Pesos (P17,000); (e) Training Pool A - Seventeen Thousand Pesos (P17,000); (f) Training Pool B - (i) Former Medalist (Team Sports/Event) - Fifteen Thousand Pesos (P15,000); and (ii) New Entries/Alternates/Sparring Partners - Ten
Thousand Two Hundred Pesos (P10,200). For athletes who garnered medals in the Olympics and World Championship shall be allowed the following allowance scheme under the Priority Athletes Program of the Commission, with the following rates: (a) Platinum - Fifty Thousand Pesos (P50,000); (b) Priority A - Forty Three Thousand Pesos (P43,000); (c) Priority B - Thirty Six Thousand Pesos (P36,000); and (d) Priority C - Thirty Three Thousand Pesos (P33,000). The scheme shall cover athletes who are qualified and endorsed by their respective National Sports Associations to be part of the said program. Implementation of this provision shall be in accordance with PSC Resolution No. 924-2024 dated September 26, 2024, PSC Board Resolution No. 692-2025 dated July 8, 2025, and such other guidelines that may be issued for the purpose.

text_A:

No. 6758, as
amended, and R.A. No. 6686, as amended; and (c) create new positions, transfer an item, or make other adjustments in the Personnel Services Itemization, whenever public interest so requires. Notwithstanding any provision of law to the contrary and within the limits of appropriations in this Act, the Ombudsman is hereby authorized to: (a) formulate and implement the Office of the Ombudsman's organizational structure; (b) fix and determine the salaries, allowances, and other benefits of personnel of the Office of the Ombudsman in accordance with the rates and levels authorized
under R.A. No. 6758, as amended, and R.A. No. 6686, as amended; and (c) create new positions, transfer an item, or make other adjustments in the Personnel Services Itemization, whenever public interest so requires. Implementation of the foregoing shall be subject to: (i) compliance with organization, staffing, and position classification and compensation standards of the DBM; (ii) scrap and build policy; and (iii) submission to DBM of a resolution stating the changes in the organization and staffing in accordance with the foregoing standards and policy for proper documentation. The officials and employees whose positions are affected by a reorganization shall be granted retirement benefits or separation pay in accordance with existing laws, which shall be payable from any unexpended balance of, or savings in the appropriations of the Office of the Ombudsman.

title: Farm-to-Mill Roads Construction Projects
text_A: Of the amounts appropriated herein, Five Hundred Million Pesos (P500,000,000) shall be used for Farm-to-Mill Road (FMR) construction projects which shall be released directly to the DPWH for the construction or rehabilitation of FMRs in key sugarcane producing provinces in accordance with the approved FMR Master Plan. For this purpose, the SRA shall ensure that: (i) the Master Plan shall include the scope of work, estimated length in kilometers, and specific location for each of the FMRs, as well as the list of priority FMR projects, which, for FMRs, must be connected to the national highways or arterial roads leading to sugarcane plantations, farms, and areas of influence; and (ii) the FMR implemented are properly geo-tagged. The approved Master Plan shall be regularly updated to prioritize: (a) sugarcane plantations of at least one hundred (100) hectares which lead to block farms, small farms, and expansion areas; (b) sugarcane farms and expansion areas of at least one hundred (100) hectares regardless of farm sizes and ownership; and (c) sugarcane area of influence of at least ten (10) hectares. Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements in accordance with applicable laws, rules, and regulations, including submission of a MOA between SRA and DPWH which shall contain the project description coverage, outline of milestones, measures of success, bill of materials, and its corresponding costs. Upon completion of the construction or rehabilitation of the FMRs, the DPWH shall turn over the management and ownership thereof to the LGUs concerned, which shall commit to shoulder the operations, repair, and maintenance costs thereof.

title: Subsidy to the National Electrification Administration
text_A:
The amount of Five Billion Six Hundred Thirty Five Million Seven Hundred Sixty Thousand Pesos (P5,635,760,000) appropriated herein under the subsidy to NEA shall be used for the implementation of the National Rural Electrification Program. The NEA is authorized to deduct engineering and administrative overhead (EAO) expenses not exceeding three percent (3%) of the project cost. The authorized EAO expenses shall be limited to: (i) pre-construction activities after detailed engineering; (ii) construction project management; (iii) testing and quality control; (iv) acquisition, rehabilitation, and repair of related equipment and parts; and (v) contingencies in relation to pre-construction activities. The EAO expenses shall be treated or booked-up as capitalized expenditures and form part of the project cost. In the implementation of the Strategized Rural Electrification and Operational Reliability for Electric Cooperatives Projects, the NEA shall observe the following: (a) Prioritize sitios where the absolute number of indigents and the incidence of poverty are high as identified in the latest official poverty statistics of the PSA as
well as those with the high probability of being energized; (b) Loans outlay to electric cooperatives shall be recorded as equity contribution of the National Government to NEA when its authorized capitalization is increased
by law, while grants thereto remain to be treated as subsidy; (c) Release funds only to electric cooperatives which have fully liquidated funds from previous years' electrification projects: Provided, That non-delinquent electric
cooperatives with ongoing projects that are not yet due for liquidation are entitled to a release of subsidy upon a new MOA with NEA subject to COA Circular
No. 2012-001: Provided, further, That electric cooperatives must completely liquidate the subsidy within three (3) months from the issuance of Certificate of
Final Inspection and Acceptance (CFIA): Provided, finally, That in cases where the electric cooperatives are not qualified to implement projects for barangay and
sitio electrification, the NEA is authorized to download the subsidy to qualified electric cooperatives in strategically located neighboring areas consistent with
the National Rural Electrification Program. The electric cooperative that implements the program shall liquidate the subsidy within three (3) months from the
issuance of CFIA. This provision shall not apply to NEA releases for calamity grants and subsidies; and (d) Prohibition on the use of subsidy for the payment of salaries, allowances, incentives, separation, or retirement benefits.

title: Operating Requirements of the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority
text_A: All income and revenues collected by the MMDA from all sources, including the national tax allotment and the mandatory remittances of component LGUs, shall be used to cover all of its operating requirements. The MMDA shall submit to the DBM, not later than November 15 of the preceding year, its detailed and consolidated operating budget for the current fiscal year. The detailed and consolidated operating budget shall reflect the MMDA's income and revenues from all sources, including its national tax allotment and the mandatory remittances of component LGUs, as well as its projected expenditures, targeted program, activities, and projects. title: Service Contracting Program for Public Transport (Intermodal and Multimodal)
text_B: The amount of Five Hundred Million Pesos (P500,000,000) appropriated herein shall be used for the implementation of a Service Contracting Program covering both land-based PUVs and maritime passenger transport services, and the modernization of maritime passenger transport services, including the promotion and use of battery electric vessels and other environment-friendly technologies, the provision of necessary support facilities, and the retrofitting of passenger vessels to improve accessibility for PWDs. The said program shall be geared towards addressing existing traffic challenges, decongesting major urban thoroughfares, and supporting the modernization of maritime transport services across the country. The program shall include both intermodal and multimodal transportation options. The Service Contracting Program shall be implemented in a manner that promotes sustainable, inclusive, and accessible public transportation. For this purpose, the DOTr shall prioritize: (a) The engagement of transport service providers utilizing BEVs or other low-emission and environment-friendly vehicle technologies; and (b) Transport units designed or retrofitted to be accessible to PWDs. The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) shall implement the land-based component of the program, while the Maritime Industry Authority (MARINA) shall implement the maritime passenger component. The DOTr, through the LTFRB and MARINA, may enter into agreements with priority LGUs to allow the direct contracting of qualified transport cooperatives, associations, corporations, or authorized maritime operators for the delivery of public transport services. The DOTr may implement a transport fee reduction or support mechanism for commuters availing of services under this program at such rates and under such conditions as will be determined by the DOTr. There shall be a mechanism for monitoring performance of operators, certifying the transport services delivered, and applying incentives and penalties, as well as systems for obtaining commuter feedback to enhance service delivery. Transparency and accountability shall be ensured through: (a) Oversight by a multi-sectoral governance committee tasked to ensure real-time feedback and ground reports for both land and maritime operations; and (b) A real-time public dashboard on the outputs and outcomes of the use of the service contracting funds. The DOTr, LTFRB, and MARINA shall issue the necessary implementing guidelines in accordance with this provision. The DOTr shall submit quarterly reports on the physical and financial accomplishments of this program to the House Committee on Appropriations and the Senate Committee on Finance, within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter. The reports shall provide the status of fund utilization, key program implementation milestones, and a comprehensive evaluation of the program's impact.
